advisory.text: A forecast update from the National Hurricane Center: full advisories every 6 hours, intermediate ones (like 14A) every 3 hours during watches and warnings.

after_action.text: What was decided, by whom and when, from the audit log. Nothing here changes a decision.

ai_run.text: One AI job, such as answering a question or drafting a report. Each is logged with its steps and cost.

ai_trace.text: The step-by-step record of a request: what was asked, what was looked up and what came back.

allowed_tools.text: The read-only lookups this AI step may use. Text-only steps have none. No step can sign or send anything.

analog_baseline.text: The typical restoration time in past storms of the same kind. SGW's estimate should beat it.

api_scope.text: What a token can read. No token can sign or change a decision.

approval.text: Who must sign, who has signed and who is still needed. Signing records your name, role and the plan version.

approval_rights.text: What each person can sign, by action and tier. Emergency approval rules are on each decision's Signatures tab.

backtest.text: Past storms run through the forecast without showing it what happened, to check how close it gets.

bad_storm.text: In 9 of 10 test storms the delay is no larger than this. It shows how bad a poor outcome can get.

breach_chance.text: Chance that pressure at the most exposed connection drops below the minimum. Above SGW's trigger (policy, not law), a boil-water notice is proposed.

break_glass.text: The Incident Commander approves alone, with a written reason. A second team must co-sign within 24 hours. Every emergency approval is reviewed.

brief_status.text: One word for how serious things are now. Set by fixed rules from outages and open deadlines, not by AI.

bwa.text: Tells customers to boil water before using it. Issued when pressure may be lost; lifted once samples test clean and the regulator agrees.

ce.text: Customers affected, weighted by need: a hospital counts for more than a household. The weights are SGW policy.

clock.text: Time left before acting is too late. It counts down to the deadline.

clock_outcome.text: Met: approved (by two signatures or alone in an emergency) by the deadline. Missed: approved later, or never.

cone.text: The area the storm's center may cross, about two-thirds of the time. Wind, rain and outages reach well beyond it.

consequence.text: When the impact is expected to begin if nothing is done. The range covers 8 in 10 storm scenarios.

copilot.text: Answers questions from SGW procedures and platform data, with sources. It only reads: it can't change, send, or sign anything.

cosign.text: After an emergency approval, a second team must co-sign within 24 hours. Late or missing co-signs are flagged here.

critical_path.text: Steps that must happen in order (1→2→3→4). A delay in any step pulls the final deadline earlier.

customer_hours.text: Customers without power multiplied by the hours they wait for a crew to arrive. Lower is better.

cv_published.text: Accuracy MIT Lincoln Laboratory reported on its own test photos; SGW didn't measure it. Photos: Civil Air Patrol via MIT Lincoln Laboratory, CC BY 4.0.

data_class_ceiling.text: The most sensitive data this AI step may see. C1 is operational data with no personal details.

decide_by.text: Latest time to decide: when impact starts minus the lead time. The range covers 8 in 10 storm scenarios.

degraded_mode.text: How much of SGW is working. M0 is normal; each step up turns off more AI and live features, down to manual procedures only.

dq_check.text: An automatic test of the data, such as ranges, units and duplicates. A failed error check blocks the dataset; a warning only flags it.

effort.text: How much the AI step may reason before answering. Higher is slower and costs more.

envelope.text: How far the plan may change without new signatures. Changes outside them need a new decision.

etr.text: When 90% of the peak customers out have power again. Publishing needs Command and Operations to sign.

etr_area.text: The estimate per crew yard's area. Still out: share of the area's peak. The bar is the 80% range; the line, the middle.

evidence.text: The records this recommendation rests on, each with its source. Open one to see where it came from and how fresh it is.

evpi.term: Most a perfect forecast could save
evpi.text: The most a perfect forecast could save, in customer-hours. If it is small, waiting for a better forecast adds little.

fan.text: Shaded bands show where outcomes could fall: the darkest holds half the scenarios, the next 8 in 10, the lightest 95 in 100.

feed_freshness.text: How old the latest data from each source is, against the maximum age SGW accepts. Older data is marked late, never shown as current.

findings_only.text: The answer failed its source check, so only the source passages are shown.

first_bad_seq.text: The earliest audit-log entry that no longer matches. Nothing from there on can be trusted.

forecast_actual.text: Forecast: what the model expects, with an 80% range. Actual: what has been measured so far in the replay.

from_platform_data.text: No AI-written text: the answer lists what platform data and procedures say, word for word.

how_i_got_this.text: What the AI looked up, in order, so you can see where the answer came from.

idle_crews.text: Early mutual-aid crews not needed because the storm turned out small. They are still paid.

kill_switch.text: Stops parts of SGW on purpose. K1 pauses signing, K2 stops the AI, K3 stops new data and decisions, and K4 turns SGW off.

lead_time.text: How long the action takes once decided. The decide-by time is when impact starts, minus this.

ledger.text: The permanent record of every decision, signature, and action. Each entry is linked to the one before, so any edit shows.

lifelines.text: Services people depend on: power, water pumping, staging yards. Counts show how many sit in high-risk counties.

lineage.text: Where this data comes from and what uses it. If a source is late, everything that uses it is affected.

loso.text: Each storm is forecast by a model built from the other storms only, so it never sees its own result.

mode_strip.text: Replay plays back a past storm on its own clock. All data is synthetic and not for operational use.

model_card.text: What a model does, which version is in use, and how it scored on new storms against a simple baseline.

mutual_aid.text: Crews lent by other utilities or contractors. Early aid is requested before landfall and is paid for whether or not the storm needs it.

no_regret.text: Whether to act now, before the next advisory, or wait. Based on the share of storm scenarios that need this action.

no_regret_act_now.text: Most scenarios need it, or waiting would miss the deadline.

no_regret_wait.text: The next NHC advisory comes before the earliest deadline, so waiting costs nothing.

not_in_documents.text: Nothing in SGW documents or platform data answers the question, so the AI says so instead of guessing.

notary.text: A separate key confirms the latest audit-log entry. Confirmed means it matches a saved checkpoint; not confirmed means it couldn't be checked.

outage_risk.text: Chance that at least 1 in 10 customers in a county lose power at the peak of the storm.

outage_surge.text: A county where outages rose far above usual, flagged by an automatic detector on public outage data. It also raises false alarms.

p50.text: Middle estimate: half of the scenarios come out lower, half higher.

page_admin.text: Who can sign what, the policy values, integrations, the audit log and AI settings. Everything here is read-only.

page_brief.text: The first page for executives: overall status, four numbers, decisions needing two teams, what changed and a draft situation report. Numbers come from platform data.

page_crews.text: Where crews are, the crew plan options compared, damage photos waiting for review, staging yards and generators.

page_water.text: Pressure in each zone, the PS-17 steps in order, boil-water notices and the sensor checks. Every decision named here opens in Decisions.

pipeline_run.text: One pass that fetches, checks and stores data from a source. Rows held back failed a check and are left out.

plan_envelope.text: How far the crew plan may change. Inside them, one person confirms; outside them, two teams sign again.

plan_scenarios.term: Planning for a range of outcomes
plan_scenarios.text: Each plan is tested against many possible storm sizes, not one average storm. Results are customer-hours of delay, averaged over test storms.

policy_chip.text: A value SGW chose for this exercise, not a regulation. Admin → Policies shows where it comes from.

policy_param.text: A number SGW chose by policy, not a legal limit. Read-only; changing one needs a decision and signatures.

pressure_floor.text: Lowest pressure allowed at a service connection. Falling below it can trigger a boil-water notice. Each state sets its own minimum.

promote.text: Confirming makes the draft the current situation report; one person confirms. Nothing is sent outside SGW.

range80.text: 8 in 10 outcomes should fall inside this range.

read_only.text: The AI reads data and writes text. It can't sign, send, change records, or start anything.

readiness.text: Pre-season checks that crews, fuel, agreements, and equipment are ready. Each item not ready has an owner and a due date.

readiness_status.text: Ready: proof is on file. Not ready: proof is missing or overdue. No record: nothing logged yet.

recall.text: Share of test faults the checks caught. Missed faults stay hidden, so a low catch rate is a real risk.

review_draft.text: AI drafts the after-action review from the audit log. Every number has a source. Nothing is filed.

sc_report.text: A draft of the interruption report South Carolina requires after a long outage. Nothing is filed from here; the filer adds notice times.

scope.text: The event and service area this view covers. Read-only in this release.

scorecard.text: How far each ETR was from what happened. The actual is simulated, so this is practice, not field proof.

seeded_faults.text: Faults added on purpose to simulated sensor data to see what the checks catch. Not field results.

sgw_trigger.text: SGW's own trigger level, set by policy, not by law. Above it, the platform proposes a boil-water notice.

sitrep.text: A short written summary of the situation. The AI drafts it; every number has a named source. A person must confirm it.

source_badge.text: The small label after a sentence names the document it came from. Select it to read the passage.

staging_yard.text: A site near likely damage where crews and equipment wait before the storm, ready to move once winds drop.

synthetic.text: Made-up data shaped like SGW's real data. Real data replaces it when SGW goes live.

system_metrics.text: Requests and response times, counted by the platform itself. Grafana adds charts when monitoring runs.

tamper_demo.text: Changes one entry on a copy of the audit log and runs the check. The real log is never touched.

tier.text: How many people must sign. Tier 1: one person confirms. Tier 2: one approver signs. Tier 3: two approvers from two teams sign.

tier_T0.text: Tier 0. Looking, asking and what-ifs. Logged; no signature needed.

tier_T1.text: Tier 1. One person confirms a draft. Also covers changes inside an already approved plan.

tier_T2.text: Tier 2. One approver from the named team must sign.

tier_T3.text: Tier 3. Two approvers from two different teams must sign. The person who proposed it can't sign.

tier_T4.text: Tier 4. Not available in SGW. The system never controls field equipment directly.

triage_score.text: How much damage the model sees in a photo, from 0 to 1. It sets the review order; a person checks every photo.

two_function_restore.text: Turning a stopped part back on needs two teams to sign, each with their password. Both signatures go in the audit log.

unverified_record.text: A field report or ticket nobody has checked yet. Treat it as unconfirmed, never as procedure.

verify_chain.text: Rechecks every entry from the first one and shows the first entry that doesn't match, if any.

version_void.text: A new advisory changed the plan, so earlier signatures no longer count. Review the new version and sign again.

vss.term: Saved by planning for the full range
vss.text: Customer-hours saved by planning for the full range of storm outcomes, not just the middle forecast. If small, crew numbers matter more than locations.

webhook.text: A web address SGW notifies when a decision changes. Failed sends retry, then stop and are listed here.

what_if.text: Reruns the storm with one thing changed, such as its track. Prepared in advance; the real plan doesn't change.

why.text: The advice, up to three reasons, and what would change it.

wind_gust.text: Strongest gust in the official forecast for each county, in mph.

wind_rule.text: A simple baseline: outages start above a wind speed fitted on the other storms. The forecast must beat it to earn its place.
